kb_entries.structure: YAML frontmatter (id, date, team, category, tags, builds_on, status, confidence) + Markdown body with sections (Context, Method, Result, Lessons Learned, Recommendations, Tools Created)
kb_entries.embedding_strategy: Chunk by major sections (## headings). Each chunk gets title + section heading prepended for context. Short entries (<2000 chars) embedded whole. Long entries (e.g. KB-0015 at ~15k chars) split into 5-10 chunks.
kb_entries.text_to_embed: For each chunk: '{title} - {section_heading}: {section_body}'. Frontmatter tags and category are metadata-only, not embedded.

team_session_logs.structure: YAML frontmatter (team_id, date, members, objective, parent_team, builds_on_knowledge) + Markdown body with sections (Objective, Approach, Decisions Made, Knowledge Generated, Artifacts Produced, Handoff Notes)
team_session_logs.embedding_strategy: Embed as a single record per log since most are under 3000 chars. For the rare long log, chunk by ## section. Always prepend objective to each chunk.

scripts.structure: Python files with module docstring (purpose, usage examples) + function/class definitions with docstrings
scripts.embedding_strategy: Embed the module docstring as primary chunk (captures purpose and usage). Optionally embed each top-level function/class docstring as a separate chunk with filename prepended. Do NOT embed raw code — it adds noise for semantic search.

sops.structure: JSON with fields: id, version, title, purpose, builds_on, plus nested section objects with title/description/rules or steps
sops.embedding_strategy: Embed the title + purpose as one chunk. Embed each top-level section (section_1_*, section_2_*, etc.) as separate chunks with SOP title prepended. Section content is flattened from nested JSON to readable text.

data_sources.structure: JSON with fields: id, name, url, api_docs_url, data_types, access_type, auth_method, rate_limits, response_format, reliability, notes, added_by_team
data_sources.embedding_strategy: Embed as a single record per source — they are small. Combine name + data_types + notes into the embedded text since these carry the semantic meaning.

table_schema.design_decision: Single unified table. Rationale: (1) enables cross-type semantic search in one query, (2) LanceDB handles filtering efficiently via metadata columns, (3) avoids query-time table joins or multi-table fan-out, (4) all document types share the same embedding space so cross-type similarity is meaningful.

doc_type.description: One of: kb_entry, team_log, script, sop, data_source

doc_id.description: Source document ID (KB-0001, TEAM-0020, SOP-022, SRC-0001, or filename for scripts)

chunk_index.description: 0-based chunk index within the document. 0 for single-chunk documents.

section_heading.description: Section heading for chunked documents, empty string for single-chunk docs

text.description: The raw text that was embedded (for display in search results and re-ranking)

vector.description: Embedding vector. Dimension 384 for all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (recommended) or 768 for all-mpnet-base-v2. Choose based on available compute.

date.description: ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD) from frontmatter or file modification. Enables temporal filtering.

team.description: Team ID that created the document (TEAM-0001, ANALYSIS-001, etc.)

category.description: Category from KB frontmatter (optimization, methodology, integration, etc.) or SOP domain. Empty for other types.

tags.description: Tags array from KB frontmatter. Empty list for non-KB types.

file_path.description: Relative path from repo root to the source file

builds_on.description: IDs of documents this builds on (KB entries, SOPs). Enables knowledge graph traversal.

rules.method: Split on ## headings. Each section becomes one chunk. If a section exceeds 2000 chars, split on paragraph boundaries (double newline) with 200-char overlap. Prepend document title to every chunk.
Embed whole if under 3000 chars. Otherwise split on ## headings. Prepend objective to every chunk.
Chunk 1: module docstring (always). Additional chunks: one per top-level function/class that has a docstring longer than 50 chars. Skip raw code.
Chunk 1: title + purpose. Additional chunks: one per top-level section key (section_1_*, section_2_*, etc.). Flatten nested JSON to readable text before embedding.
Single chunk per source. Concatenate name, notes, and data_types into one text block.

usage_patterns: Filter by doc_type to search only KB entries or only SOPs
Filter by team to find all artifacts from a specific team session
Filter by category for domain-specific KB searches
Filter by tags for fine-grained topic matching (complements semantic search)
Filter by date range for temporal queries (e.g., 'what was learned today')
Use builds_on for knowledge graph traversal after initial semantic match

estimated_total_records.growth_projection: Repository adds ~5-15 docs per team session. At 5 sessions/day, expect ~25-75 new docs/day or ~75-375 new records/day. LanceDB handles millions of records so this is well within capacity.

primary.reason: Fast, small, good quality for English text. Runs on CPU in <1s for 500 records. Available via sentence-transformers.

alternative.reason: Higher quality embeddings at 2x dimension cost. Use if search quality with MiniLM is insufficient.

embedding_model_recommendations.note: If using the Gemini embeddings API (SRC-0036 in sources), dimension is 768 and requires API key. Prefer local models for zero-dependency operation.

query_patterns.semantic_search: Embed query text, find top-K nearest neighbors in vector column. Optionally pre-filter by doc_type, team, or category.
query_patterns.hybrid_search: Combine vector similarity with FTS on the text column (LanceDB supports this natively). Improves recall for exact-match terms.
query_patterns.knowledge_graph_walk: After finding a relevant KB entry, follow its builds_on links to retrieve related entries. Then find other docs by the same team.
query_patterns.temporal_search: Filter by date range, then rank by vector similarity. Useful for 'what did we learn recently about X'.
query_patterns.cross_type_discovery: Search without doc_type filter to find connections across KB entries, SOPs, scripts, and data sources about the same topic.
